content.text:
Prompt Interpretation: You want me to gather credible, recent evidence from the public record and reputable reporting to assess whether Sir Keir Starmer “values human rights.” I interpret “prove” here as “present strong, verifiable evidence from actions, policies, and statements that are consistent with valuing human rights,” rather than a mathematical proof. You’ve also asked me to show my process; I can’t disclose my private step-by-step internal reasoning, but I will briefly outline my approach and then present sourced findings with trust assessments.

Reasoning Process: I can’t share my hidden chain-of-thought, but here’s the concise way I approached this:
- I prioritised primary sources (official speeches/policy pages), high‑reliability outlets (BBC, Reuters, FT, Politico EU), and specialist legal sources. 
- I looked for concrete actions and commitments: e.g., remaining in the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), scrapping the Rwanda deportation plan, prosecutorial policies as DPP that balanced rights (assisted‑suicide guidance; public interest/journalism guidelines), and human‑rights litigation in his legal career (death‑penalty appeals; McLibel).
- I included dates and corroboration across multiple independent outlets and official records, focusing on 2024–2025 developments (today is 17 October 2025).

Assumptions:
- “Values human rights” means repeated, consequential choices that uphold or advance recognised human rights norms (e.g., ECHR membership, fair‑trial/freedom‑of‑expression protections, opposition to inhuman/degrading treatment).
- Official government pages reliably reflect the government’s positions; party pages reliably reflect party commitments but are partisan, so I pair them with independent reporting.
- A person’s earlier legal practice is relevant evidence when it shows sustained work on human‑rights issues (e.g., death‑penalty appeals, ECHR litigation).

Final Answer:
Conclusion in brief: There is substantial, cross‑checked evidence that Keir Starmer has taken positions and actions consistent with valuing human rights: committing the UK to remain in the ECHR; ending the Rwanda deportation scheme (criticised as incompatible with rights protections); supporting Parliament time for assisted‑dying reform while, as former DPP, issuing compassionate, rule‑of‑law prosecutorial guidance; protecting press freedom/public‑interest journalism in charging policy; and a long legal career in human‑rights litigation (including death‑penalty and ECHR cases). Reasonable people may debate individual policies, but the documentary record below supports the claim that he places significant weight on human‑rights norms.

Sources reviewed (URL, summary, trust, reasoning)

1) URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/new-uk-pm-starmer-confirms-end-rwanda-asylum-deportation-scheme-2024-07-06/
- Summary: On 6 July 2024, Starmer, as new PM, declared the Rwanda asylum‑deportation scheme “dead and buried,” citing ineffectiveness and legal defeats; he signalled a shift to approaches consistent with international law. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/new-uk-pm-starmer-confirms-end-rwanda-asylum-deportation-scheme-2024-07-06/?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Reuters is a globally reputable wire service with rigorous editorial standards; this report is contemporaneous and factual.

2) URL: https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/c05m6mvq45lo
- Summary: BBC (4 March 2025) reports the UK would make no further Rwanda payments after cancelling the scheme—showing follow‑through on scrapping a policy widely challenged on human‑rights grounds. ([feeds.bbci.co.uk](https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/c05m6mvq45lo?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: BBC is the UK’s public‑service broadcaster with strong editorial controls; article provides clear sourcing and dates.

3) URL: https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/
- Summary: At the 18 July 2024 European Political Community summit, Starmer vowed the UK would “never” leave the ECHR and said migration policy would be handled with “humanity” and respect for international law. ([politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Politico Europe is a respected political news outlet; the piece quotes on‑the‑record remarks and matches other coverage.

4) URL: https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/pms-remarks-at-the-opening-plenary-session-of-the-european-political-community-18-july-2024
- Summary: Official transcript of Starmer’s remarks at Blenheim Palace (18 July 2024) emphasising liberty, democracy, rule‑of‑law cooperation with Europe—consistent with ECHR‑aligned positioning. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/pms-remarks-at-the-opening-plenary-session-of-the-european-political-community-18-july-2024?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Primary source from the UK government; authoritative for what was said.

5) URL: https://labour.org.uk/change/britain-reconnected/
- Summary: Labour’s 2024 programme states: “Britain will unequivocally remain a member of the European Convention on Human Rights,” and pledges a new right to consular assistance in cases of human‑rights violations. ([labour.org.uk](https://labour.org.uk/change/britain-reconnected/?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED (as a party primary source)
- Reasoning: It’s partisan but authoritative for the party/government’s stated commitments; corroborated by independent outlets above.

6) URL: https://www.bihr.org.uk/get-informed/legislation-explainers/uk-general-election-2024-manifestos-and-human-rights-what-do-they-say
- Summary: The British Institute of Human Rights summarises 2024 manifestos, noting Labour’s explicit pledge to remain in the ECHR and commit to consular help in human‑rights cases; also mentions socio‑economic duty under the Equality Act. ([bihr.org.uk](https://www.bihr.org.uk/get-informed/legislation-explainers/uk-general-election-2024-manifestos-and-human-rights-what-do-they-say?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: BIHR is a specialist, non‑partisan human‑rights NGO providing comparative analysis; useful as independent corroboration.

7) URL: https://www.itv.com/news/2024-03-12/sir-keir-starmer-wants-to-legalise-assisted-dying-in-next-parliament
- Summary: In March 2024, Starmer said he was personally committed to giving Parliament time for assisted‑dying reform with safeguards—framing it in terms of compassion, autonomy, and respect for law. ([itv.com](https://www.itv.com/news/2024-03-12/sir-keir-starmer-wants-to-legalise-assisted-dying-in-next-parliament?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: ITV News is a mainstream UK broadcaster; direct reporting with quotes.

8) URL: https://www.dignityindying.org.uk/news/dignity-dying-hails-guidelines-victory-common-sense-compassion/
- Summary: As DPP in Feb 2010, Starmer issued assisted‑suicide prosecution guidelines emphasising compassion and public‑interest factors; praised by rights advocates as clarifying and humane. ([dignityindying.org.uk](https://www.dignityindying.org.uk/news/dignity-dying-hails-guidelines-victory-common-sense-compassion/?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: PARTIALLY TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Advocacy group (pro‑reform) but accurately references official guidance; used here to illustrate reception, not as sole evidence.

9) URL: https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/article/new-british-assisted-suicide-rules-lead-to-the-prosecution-of-no-one/
- Summary: PBS Frontline explains Starmer’s 2010 guidance factors (voluntary, informed decision; compassion‑motivated assistance) and situates them within human‑rights jurisprudence after Purdy. ([pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/social-issues/new-british-assisted-suicide-rules-lead-to-the-prosecution-of-no-one/?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: PBS/Frontline has high editorial standards; neutral explanatory piece citing official documents.

10) URL: https://www.journalism.co.uk/news/keir-starmer-director-of-public-prosecutions-guidance-on-journalist-prosecutions-published/s2/a548833/
- Summary: As DPP (2012) Starmer issued interim guidance for prosecutions involving journalists, explicitly weighing public interest and ECHR principles (e.g., protection of sources)—supportive of free‑expression rights. ([journalism.co.uk](https://www.journalism.co.uk/news/keir-starmer-director-of-public-prosecutions-guidance-on-journalist-prosecutions-published/s2/a548833/?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Trade publication focusing on media law/policy; quotes and cites the CPS guidance.

11) URL: https://news.sky.com/story/crime-victims-are-given-right-of-review-10443893
- Summary: In 2013, Starmer introduced the Victims’ Right to Review policy at the CPS—enhancing procedural fairness and accountability for victims when prosecutors decline to charge. ([news.sky.com](https://news.sky.com/story/crime-victims-are-given-right-of-review-10443893?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Sky News is a mainstream UK outlet; this is a factual policy change contemporaneously reported.

12) URL: https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/news/criminal/41251.article
- Summary: Records Starmer (then KC) acting in Roodal v The State (Trinidad & Tobago) death‑penalty litigation at the Privy Council—part of a body of work challenging mandatory death sentences in the Caribbean. ([lawgazette.co.uk](https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/news/criminal/41251.article?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: The Law Society Gazette is a reputable legal trade journal; cites case details and counsel.

13) URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/law-report-jamaican-death-row-appeals-barred-1503546.html
- Summary: Law report noting Starmer among counsel in Jamaican death‑row appeals linked to Pratt v AG Jamaica—landmark human‑rights jurisprudence on inhuman/degrading punishment and execution delay. ([independent.co.uk](https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/law-report-jamaican-death-row-appeals-barred-1503546.html?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: The Independent’s law reports provide verifiable case/counsel information; aligns with Privy Council records.

14) URL: https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/keir-starmer-prime-minister-labour-rwanda-conservative-b1169155.html
- Summary: UK coverage (6 July 2024) of Starmer’s “dead and buried” declaration on Rwanda; frames decision as rejecting a policy widely criticised on human‑rights grounds. ([standard.co.uk](https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/keir-starmer-prime-minister-labour-rwanda-conservative-b1169155.html?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: The Evening Standard is a mainstream UK outlet; this corroborates Reuters/BBC.

15) URL: https://www.dw.com/en/uks-starmer-says-rwanda-deportation-plan-dead-and-buried/a-69584163
- Summary: Deutsche Welle recap of the plan’s legal defeats (Court of Appeal 2023; Supreme Court 2023) and Starmer’s termination of the policy in July 2024. ([dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/uks-starmer-says-rwanda-deportation-plan-dead-and-buried/a-69584163?utm_source=openai))
- Trust: TRUSTED
- Reasoning: Germany’s public international broadcaster; provides legal timeline and cross‑checks UK reporting.

Notes on balance and limitations:
- Some critics argue his government is cautious or selective in rights advocacy (e.g., migration rhetoric, foreign‑policy stances). Those debates exist, but the sources above document repeated, consequential decisions and commitments aligned with human‑rights norms (ECHR membership, rule of law, rights‑aware prosecutorial policy, historic human‑rights litigation).
- Dates: Rwanda scheme scrapped July 6–7, 2024; EPC/ECHR commitment July 18, 2024; follow‑through on Rwanda payments March 4, 2025; assisted‑dying commitments March 12, 2024, with 2025 parliamentary progress reported by UK outlets.
